modes.title: Hi-Res Mode (280×192)
modes.desc: The Apple II Hi-Res mode provides 280×192 resolution with 6 colors. Colors are determined by horizontal position and pixel patterns due to NTSC artifact coloring.
modes.best: Classic Apple II graphics, games, and artwork that need authentic period look
opts: Error diffusion works well. Floyd-Steinberg recommended for photos.
Perceptive matching gives best results with the limited palette.

header: Super Hi-Res graphics with up to 3200 colors

modes.title: 3200 Colors (Brooks)
modes.desc: True 3200-color mode using the Brooks format. Each of the 200 scanlines has its own independent 16-color palette, allowing up to 3,200 unique colors on screen.
modes.best: Photographic images, gradients, images with many colors
opts: Controls palette reuse between similar scanlines. Higher values reduce banding but may lose color accuracy. Set to 0 for maximum color fidelity, 10-20 for balanced results.
All dithering algorithms work well. Floyd-Steinberg is recommended for photos.
Increase to compensate for the IIgs's somewhat muted palette.

modes.title: 256 Colors (16 Palettes)
modes.desc: Standard SHR format with 16 palette slots. Scanlines are grouped and share palettes. Maximum 256 unique colors (16 palettes × 16 colors).
modes.best: Compatibility with standard SHR viewers, when file size matters
opts: Which of the 16 palettes each scanline uses. Banded: 16 even bands of lines. Palette Reuse: the older method, which reuses the previous line's palette when it fits well enough; on photos it usually looks worse than Banded. Per-Line: any line can use any palette, so similar lines share one even when they're far apart; usually the best quality.
Only visible with 'Palette Reuse'. Controls how similar scanlines must be to share a palette.

modes.title: 320×200 (16 Colors)
modes.desc: Standard Super Hi-Res mode with a single 16-color palette for the entire image. Classic IIgs graphics mode.
modes.best: Simple graphics, logos, images with limited color range
opts: Essential for this mode. Atkinson gives a classic Mac look, Floyd-Steinberg for smoother results.

modes.title: 640×200 (4 Colors)
modes.desc: High-resolution mode with 640 horizontal pixels but only 4 colors. Good for text and line art.
modes.best: Screenshots, text-heavy images, technical drawings
opts: Ordered (Bayer) dithering works well to avoid artifacts.

modes.title: 640×200 Enhanced (16 Colors)
modes.desc: Enhanced 640 mode using column-aware dithering. Even columns use one 4-color sub-palette, odd columns use another, for 8 effective colors.
modes.best: Higher resolution images that need more color variety

modes.title: 640×200 Desktop (16 Colors)
modes.desc: Uses the GS/OS Finder palette with column-aware dithering. Even columns: Black, Blue, Yellow, White. Odd columns: Black, Red, Green, White.
modes.best: Images that should match the GS/OS desktop aesthetic
opts: All algorithms work, but results will be limited to the fixed Finder palette.

modes.title: HiRes Mode (320×200)
modes.desc: Standard C64 bitmap mode with 320×200 resolution. Each 8×8 character cell can use 2 colors from the 16-color palette.
modes.best: High detail images, line art, text
opts: Error diffusion recommended. Floyd-Steinberg or Atkinson work well.
Perceptive gives natural results, Luma preserves brightness detail.

modes.title: Multicolor Mode (160×200)
modes.desc: C64 multicolor bitmap with double-wide pixels. Each 4×8 character cell can use 4 colors: 3 from the palette + 1 shared background color.
modes.best: Colorful images, photos, artwork with many color areas
opts: Average: Blends adjacent pixels for smoother results. Brightest: Picks the brighter pixel, preserves highlights.
Ordered dithering (Bayer) often works better than error diffusion in multicolor mode.

modes.title: PETSCII Mode (40×25)
modes.desc: Character-based graphics using the C64's built-in PETSCII character set. 40×25 character cells (320×200 pixels). Each 8×8 cell displays one of 256 PETSCII characters with 2 colors: global background + per-cell foreground.
modes.best: ASCII/ANSI-style art, BBS graphics, text-based imagery, retro terminal aesthetics
opts: XOR-based algorithm finds the best matching PETSCII character for each 8×8 tile.
Background: most common dark color. Foreground: most contrasting color per cell.
Perceptive matching recommended for best character/color selection.

modes.title: HiRes Mode (176×184)
modes.desc: VIC-20 high-resolution mode using custom character set. 22×23 character cells, each 8×8 pixels with 2 colors per cell.
modes.best: Detailed images, line art, higher resolution needs
opts: Error diffusion works well with the limited 2 colors per cell.
Perceptive recommended for natural color selection.

modes.title: LowRes Mode (88×184)
modes.desc: VIC-20 multicolor mode with double-wide pixels. 22×23 cells, each 4×8 pixels with 4 colors: background, border, auxiliary + 1 per cell.
modes.best: Colorful images, photos, artwork needing more colors per area
opts: Average: Blends pixels for smoother look. Brightest: Preserves highlight detail.
Ordered dithering often works better than error diffusion.

modes.title: Standard Mode (256×192)
modes.desc: ZX Spectrum screen with 256×192 pixels. Each 8×8 attribute cell has 2 colors (ink + paper) from the 15-color palette. Famous for 'attribute clash' when colors cross cell boundaries.
modes.best: Authentic Spectrum look, pixel art, images with clearly defined color regions
opts: Works within attribute constraints. Floyd-Steinberg or Atkinson recommended.
CLAHE or SWAHE can help improve detail in attribute-constrained images.
Perceptive gives natural results within the limited palette.

modes.title: Mode 1 (320×200, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Standard CPC mode with 320×200 resolution and 4 colors selected from the 27-color hardware palette. Good balance of resolution and color.
modes.best: General purpose graphics, games, detailed images
opts: Error diffusion recommended. Floyd-Steinberg or Atkinson work well.
The converter automatically selects optimal 4 colors from 27.

modes.title: Mode 0 (160×200, 16 colors)
modes.desc: Low-resolution CPC mode with double-wide pixels. Uses all 16 palette entries, selected from 27 hardware colors. Most colorful CPC mode.
modes.best: Colorful images, photos, artwork needing many colors
opts: Average: Blends adjacent pixels. Brightest: Picks brighter pixel for highlights.
Ordered dithering often gives better results than error diffusion in this mode.

modes.title: HiRes Mode (320×200)
modes.desc: Plus/4 high-resolution bitmap mode with 320×200 pixels. Each 8×8 character cell can use 2 colors from the 128-color TED palette.
modes.best: Detailed images, line art, high resolution needs
opts: Error diffusion works well. Floyd-Steinberg recommended.
The large 128-color palette provides excellent color matching. Perceptive recommended.

modes.title: Multicolor Mode (160×200)
modes.desc: Plus/4 multicolor bitmap with double-wide pixels. Each 4×8 character cell can use 4 colors: 2 global colors + 2 per cell from the 128-color palette.
modes.best: Colorful photos, artwork with smooth gradients
opts: Average: Blends adjacent pixels smoothly. Brightest: Preserves highlight detail.
Both error diffusion and ordered dithering work well with the large palette.

modes.title: Low Res (320×200, 16 colors)
modes.desc: Atari ST low-resolution mode with 320×200 pixels and 16 colors selected from the 512-color hardware palette. Uses 4 bitplanes. Standard mode for colorful graphics.
modes.best: General graphics, photos, colorful images
opts: Bayer 4×4 is default. Error diffusion (Floyd-Steinberg, Atkinson) also works well.
Perceptive recommended. The converter automatically selects optimal 16 colors from 512.

modes.title: Medium Res (640×200, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Atari ST medium-resolution mode with 640×200 pixels and 4 colors selected from the 512-color hardware palette. Uses 2 bitplanes. Good balance of resolution and color.
modes.best: Text, line art, graphics needing higher horizontal resolution
opts: Ordered dithering (Bayer) often works well with limited 4-color palette.
Perceptive recommended. Optimal 4 colors are automatically selected.

modes.title: High Res (640×400, Monochrome)
modes.desc: Atari ST high-resolution mode with 640×400 pixels in monochrome (2 colors: black and white). Uses 1 bitplane. Requires a dedicated high-res monitor on original hardware.
modes.best: Text, CAD, desktop publishing, high-detail line art
opts: Bayer dithering creates good halftone patterns. Floyd-Steinberg for photographs.
CLAHE or HE can help improve detail in photos before conversion.

modes.title: Graphics 8 (320×192, 2 colors)
modes.desc: High-resolution monochrome mode. 320×192 pixels with 2 colors (background + foreground). Best for line art and high-contrast images.
modes.best: Line art, text, high contrast images
opts: Bayer dithering creates good patterns in monochrome.
HE or CLAHE can improve detail in photos.

modes.title: Graphics 15 (160×192, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Medium-resolution mode with 160×192 pixels and 4 colors from the 128-color palette. Double-wide pixels. Most versatile mode for general images.
modes.best: General graphics, photos, colorful images
opts: Bayer 4×4 is default. Floyd-Steinberg also works well.

modes.title: Graphics 9 (80×192, 16 shades)
modes.desc: GTIA mode with 80×192 pixels and 16 shades of grayscale. Quad-wide pixels. Excellent for photographic images.
modes.best: Photos, portraits, grayscale images
opts: Minimal dithering often best. Try Floyd-Steinberg for smoother gradients.
CLAHE can enhance detail in low-contrast photos.

modes.title: Graphics 10 (80×192, 9 colors)
modes.desc: GTIA color mode with 80×192 pixels and 9 colors selected from the 128-color palette. Quad-wide pixels. Good for colorful images with limited detail needs.
modes.best: Colorful low-res images, artistic graphics
opts: Bayer dithering recommended. Error diffusion may produce visible artifacts.
Perceptive recommended for natural color selection from the 128-color palette.

modes.title: Graphics 11 (80×192, 16 hues)
modes.desc: GTIA hue mode with 80×192 pixels and 16 different hues at one luminance level. Quad-wide pixels. All colors have the same brightness.
modes.best: Images with many different colors but uniform brightness, artistic effects
opts: Bayer dithering works well. Hue-based dithering preserves color variety.
All 16 colors share the same luminance, so contrast comes from hue differences only.

modes.title: Mode 0 (640×256, 2 colors)
modes.desc: High-resolution monochrome mode with 640×256 pixels. 2 colors selected from the 8-color palette. 80 bytes per line.
modes.best: Text, line art, high-resolution graphics
opts: Bayer dithering creates good patterns in 2-color mode.
HE or CLAHE can improve detail in photos.

modes.title: Mode 1 (320×256, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Medium-resolution mode with 320×256 pixels. 4 colors selected from the 8-color palette. Good balance of resolution and color.
modes.best: General graphics, games, colorful images
opts: Perceptive recommended for natural color selection.

modes.title: Mode 2 (160×256, 8 colors)
modes.desc: Low-resolution mode with 160×256 pixels and all 8 colors available. Quad-wide pixels. Most colorful BBC Micro mode.
modes.best: Colorful images, photos, artwork needing full palette
opts: Often not needed with 8 colors. Light dithering can help gradients.
Hue matching preserves colors well with this saturated palette.

modes.title: Mode 4 (320×256, 2 colors)
modes.desc: Medium-resolution monochrome mode. Same resolution as Mode 1 but with only 2 colors, using half the memory.
modes.best: Line art, text, when memory is limited

modes.title: Mode 5 (160×256, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Low-resolution mode with 4 colors. Same resolution as Mode 2 but with fewer colors, using half the memory.
modes.best: Colorful graphics when memory is limited

modes.title: Standard Mode (32 colors)
modes.desc: Standard Amiga OCS mode with 32 colors selected from the 4096-color hardware palette. Uses 5 bitplanes for 32 simultaneous colors.
modes.best: General graphics, games, images with limited color range
opts: Bayer 4×4 is default. Error diffusion also works well.
Perceptive recommended. Automatically selects optimal 32 colors.

modes.title: HAM6 Mode (4096 colors)
modes.desc: Hold-And-Modify mode allows up to 4096 colors on screen. Each pixel can either use a palette color or modify one RGB channel from the previous pixel. Uses 6 bitplanes.
modes.best: Photographs, gradients, images requiring many colors
opts: Usually not needed due to high color count. Subtle dithering can help with gradients.

modes.title: Standard Mode (256 colors)
modes.desc: AGA mode with 256 colors selected from the full 24-bit palette. Uses 8 bitplanes for 256 simultaneous colors.
modes.best: General graphics, games, images with moderate color range
opts: Bayer 4×4 is default. With 256 colors, less dithering is usually needed.
Perceptive recommended. Automatically selects optimal 256 colors.

modes.title: HAM8 Mode (262144 colors)
modes.desc: AGA Hold-And-Modify mode allows up to 262,144 colors on screen. Each pixel can either use a palette color or modify one RGB channel (6 bits per channel) from the previous pixel. Uses 8 bitplanes.
modes.best: Photographs, photorealistic images, gradients
opts: Rarely needed. HAM8 provides excellent color reproduction.

header: CGA, EGA, VGA and text modes

modes.title: CGA Mode (320×200, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Color Graphics Adapter mode with 4 colors from fixed palettes. The iconic PC graphics standard from 1981.
modes.best: Classic PC game graphics, retro DOS aesthetics
opts: Floyd-Steinberg strongly recommended due to limited 4-color palette.

modes.title: EGA Mode (320×200, 16 colors)
modes.desc: Enhanced Graphics Adapter mode using the standard fixed 16-color EGA palette. The same colors as CGA's 16-color text mode palette.
modes.best: Authentic EGA look, classic DOS game graphics
opts: Ordered dithering (Bayer) often produces good results. 16 colors allow reasonable color reproduction.
Hue or Chroma recommended to preserve colors with this fixed palette. Perceptive may map saturated colors to grays.

modes.title: EGA 64 Mode (320×200, 16 from 64)
modes.desc: Enhanced Graphics Adapter mode with 16 colors selected from the full 64-color EGA palette. Allows optimal color selection per image.
modes.best: Images that benefit from custom color selection, Sierra adventure games aesthetic
opts: Ordered dithering (Bayer) often produces good results.
Perceptive recommended. Optimal 16 colors are automatically selected from the 64-color EGA palette.

modes.title: VGA Mode 13h (320×200, 256 colors)
modes.desc: The legendary VGA Mode 13h with 256 colors from the full 262,144-color VGA palette. The standard for DOS games from 1987-1997.
modes.best: DOS game graphics, pixel art, photographs
opts: Often not needed with 256 colors. Use sparingly for photographs.
Uses adaptive palette generation (median cut) for optimal 256-color palette.

modes.title: CGA 80×25 Text Mode
modes.desc: Classic DOS text mode using 8×8 character cells. 80 columns × 25 rows with 16 foreground and 8 background colors. Resolution: 640×200 pixels.
modes.best: ASCII art, BBS graphics, ANSI art aesthetics
opts: Uses block characters and shading patterns to approximate image content
16 foreground colors, 8 background colors per character cell

modes.title: VESA 132×50 Text Mode
modes.desc: Extended VESA text mode with 132 columns × 50 rows. Higher resolution text display (1056×400 pixels) for more detailed ASCII art.
modes.best: High-detail ASCII art, detailed text mode graphics
opts: Same block characters as CGA text mode but with more cells for finer detail

modes.title: Screen 2 (256×192, MSX1)
modes.desc: MSX1 graphics mode using the TMS9918 video chip. 2 colors per 8×1 horizontal line from the fixed 16-color palette. Each 8-pixel horizontal segment has its own foreground and background color.
modes.best: MSX1 game graphics, colorful images with horizontal color variation
opts: Error diffusion works well within the 8×1 color constraints.
Hue or Chroma recommended to preserve colors with the fixed TMS9918 palette.

modes.title: Screen 5 (256×212, MSX2)
modes.desc: MSX2 graphics mode using the V9938 video chip. 16 colors selected from a 512-color palette (3 bits per channel). Similar to Atari ST graphics.
modes.best: MSX2 game graphics, detailed images with custom palette
opts: Floyd-Steinberg recommended for photos. Bayer for pixel art.
Perceptive recommended. Optimal 16 colors are automatically selected from 512.

modes.title: Screen 8 (256×212, MSX2)
modes.desc: MSX2 256-color mode with fixed 3-3-2 RGB palette (3 bits red, 3 bits green, 2 bits blue). No palette selection needed - colors are directly mapped.
modes.best: Photographs, images with smooth gradients
opts: Often not needed with 256 colors. Light dithering can help with banding.
Blue channel has only 4 levels (2 bits), so blue gradients may show more banding.

modes.title: PMODE 3 (128×192, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Standard CoCo graphics mode using the MC6847 VDG chip. 128×192 resolution with 4 colors from either Color Set 0 or Set 1. Most common mode for CoCo 1/2 graphics.
modes.best: General CoCo graphics, games, colorful images
opts: Green, Yellow, Blue, Red on black background
Buff, Cyan, Magenta, Orange on black background

modes.title: PMODE 4 (256×192, 2 colors)
modes.desc: High-resolution CoCo mode with 256×192 pixels but only 2 colors. Can use NTSC artifact coloring for additional colors on real hardware.
modes.best: Line art, text, high contrast images, artifact color graphics
opts: Enables NTSC artifact colors (Blue/Orange) for additional color variety on composite displays
Bayer dithering creates good patterns in 2-color mode

modes.title: PMODE 1 (128×96, 4 colors)
modes.desc: Low-resolution CoCo mode with 128×96 pixels and 4 colors. Uses less memory than other modes. Good for simple graphics.
modes.best: Simple graphics, memory-constrained applications
opts: Light dithering recommended due to low resolution

modes.title: PMODE 2 (128×192, 2 colors)
modes.desc: Medium-resolution mode with 128×192 pixels and 2 colors. Uses half the memory of PMODE 3.
modes.best: Monochrome graphics, line art when memory is limited

modes.title: CoCo 3 (320×200, 16 colors)
modes.desc: CoCo 3 GIME mode with 320×200 resolution and 16 colors from the 64-color RGB palette (2 bits per channel). Requires CoCo 3 hardware.
modes.best: Detailed colorful graphics, photos, CoCo 3 games
opts: Uses a standard 16-color palette for emulator compatibility
Floyd-Steinberg recommended for photos, Bayer for pixel art

modes.title: CoCo 3 (640×200, 4 colors)
modes.desc: CoCo 3 high-resolution mode with 640×200 pixels and 4 colors. Good balance of resolution and color for text and detailed graphics.
modes.best: Text, CAD, detailed line art, desktop applications
opts: Ordered dithering (Bayer) works well with limited 4-color palette
